articleTitle: Unidirectional printed loop antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A new type of printed rectangular loop antenna with capacitive loads is proposed for unidirectional radiation pattern production. The arrangement presented here is shown to have a current distribution with balanced magnitude and 90/spl deg/ phase difference on parallel radiating edges of the loop. As a result, the printed loop is equivalent to an array of two dipoles with quarter-wavelength space separation and 90/spl deg/ phase excitation difference. Simulated and measured results for 1 GHz center-frequency operation show that the new unidirectional printed loop antenna can achieve a front-to-back ratio of more than 20 dB, power gain of 4.5 dBi, and can be easily matched.

articleTitle: LTCC technology and its applications in high frequency front end modules
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The ongoing developments of low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technique are making it more and more attractive for applications in microwave and millimetre wave frequency band. The most active areas for high frequency applications include Bluetooth module, front end module (FEM) of mobile phones, wireless local access network (WLAN). Local multipoint distribution system (LMDS) and collision avoidance radar etc. The recent development of LTCC substrate material extend the applicable frequency of the technique up to 100GHz. Owing to the feature of low conductor loss, low substrate loss, and up to 50 laminated layers, LTCC provide a harmonic bed for embedded microwave and mm wave passive components and accessories including antennas. In addition, LTCC substrate material has a wide tuneable range of thermal expansion coefficient. It is this feature that makes the LTCC substrate very attractive for various integrated packaging. In the presentation, the present status of the technology will be reviewed, from its manufacturing process, material properties to RF and microwave performance of typical LTCC modules. The LTCC market projection and cost issue will be also discussed to have a globe view of the technology. A large number of practical examples for high frequency applications will be followed to display the current technology status. The examples include, but not limited to, (1) RF front end module for mobile phones, (2) antennas for WLAN and Bluetooth devices, (3) laminated waveguide and other new form of transmission lines for mm wave applications, (4) integrated mm wave antenna arrays, and (5) Integrated RF modules such as high performance VCO. balanced LNA, miniaturized RF filters and balun. Since the most challenge issue in LTCC module designs is the integrated passives, the emphasis of the examples will be placed on the embedded passives and system integration. Some practical LTCC modules developed in The Chinese University of Hong Kong are listed in the following. The details of these modules can be found in the listed references and will be further elaborated in the presentation.

articleTitle: An overview of self-calibration in sensor array processing
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The performance of high-resolution DOA estimation methods seriously degenerates when there are model errors in array manifold. According to various prior knowledge of array manifold, this paper classifies series of array self-calibration methods based on second order statistics, then discusses them and concludes their advantages and disadvantages, finally gives some prospect for research on self-calibration.

articleTitle: Microstrip log periodic antenna using circuit simulator
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper described the method of designing the quasi log periodically scaled microstrip antenna using S parameter of the antenna and microstrip transmission line circuit. The novelty of this antenna structure is a combination of a small number of elements to create a log periodic array with modest bandwidth. The radiating element is a square patch antenna. The input impedance of the patch is adjusted to the inset feed and matched at 50 ohm impedance. This antenna has been analysed for five, seven and nine elements array. The performance of the antenna is compared using Momentum (MoM) simulator. The scaling factor of 1.05 has been chosen for design.

articleTitle: Research on the radiation characteristics of the leaky coaxial cables
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The leaky coaxial cable (LCX) with vertical periodic slots is considered as an antenna array. By superposition principle, the field distributions of the LCX both in radial and axis directions are analyzed, the radiation patterns for near and far regions of the cable are studied. The relationships between the field distributions and the radiation modes are discussed. In addition, the field distribution and fluctuation of a discrete antenna system are also studied in terms of the theory of LCX for comparison.

articleTitle: Design of smart antenna testbed prototype
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The use of wireless, mobile, a personal communications service is expanding rapidly. Market projections indicate that within ten years approximately 50% of the total teletraffic (including voice, FAX and multimedia data) is handled via mobile communication networks. Adaptive or "smart" antenna arrays can further increase channel capacity through spatial division. Adaptive antennas an also track mobile users, improving both signal range and quality. For these reasons, smart antenna systems have attracted widespread interest in the telecommunications industry for applications to third generation wireless systems. The problems in 3G systems can be effectively tackled by using smart antennas. This paper aims to design and develop an advanced antennas testbed to serve as a common reference for testing adaptive antenna arrays and signal combining algorithms, as well as complete systems. The goal of this paper is to develop low complexity smart antenna structures for 3G systems. The emphasis is laid on ease of implementation in a multichannel/multi-user environment. A smart antenna test bed is developed, and various state-of-the-art DSP structures and algorithms are investigated. Some of the benefits that can be achieved by using SAS (smart antenna system) include lower mobile terminal power consumption, range extension, ISI reduction, higher data rate support, and ease of integration into the existing base station system. In terms of economic benefits, adaptive antenna systems employed at base station, though increases the per base station cost, can increase coverage area of each cell site, thereby reducing the total system cost dramatically - often by more than 50% without compromising the system performance. The testbed can be employed to illustrate enhancement of system capacity and service quality in wireless communications applications.

articleTitle: A cavity backed rectangular patch antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Cavity backing of the conventional rectangular microstrip antenna is being proposed. The proposed antennas have been simulated. An input impedance of 71 % for VSWR /spl les/ 2.00 has been obtained from the proposed antenna. Results obtained for the cavity backed and without cavity backed antenna has been compared. It has been found that by cavity backing the conventional antenna bandwidth increases many times.

articleTitle: Research on RCS measurement under non-far field condition
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: While stealth technologies for large scale targets were researched, RCS static measurement method was adopted, which is often used under non-far field condition. Therefore a theoretical premise was deduced, and a stepped frequency pulse compression system was designed for RCS measurement, especially a novel RF channel was designed to keep the system stable. Not only the simulation but also the experimental result is presented LU the paper; at the same time, some practical difficulties are designated.

articleTitle: The state-of-the- art of the statistical theory of antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In the paper the author set forth foundations of the theory of antenna arrays with randomness in excitation and position of radiators. Main attention is paid to problems of the analysis of statistical characteristics of similar arrays in the far zone. The theoretical generalization to the Fresnel zone both for equidistant and non-equidistant arrays is given along with problems in the analysis (direct problems), the inverse problems - the problems of the statistical synthesis of antenna arrays. The most important literature characterizing the state-of-the-art in the statistical theory of antenna arrays is indicated.

articleTitle: A high directivity patch antenna using a PBG cover together with a PBG substrate
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A high directivity patch antenna using a photonic bandgap (PBG) cover together with a PBG substrate is designed. The input return loss, radiation pattern and directivity of this antenna are studied by the finite-difference time-domain method. The directivity of the PBG antenna is greatly improved. Experimental results are also reported to verify the design.

articleTitle: On the performance of genetic algorithm based adaptive beamforming
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper we present the detailed performance of GA-ABF technique (genetic algorithm based adaptive beamforming) under different interference/noise environment. First, the GA-ABF's performance under stationary scenario is analyzed in terms of different interferences power, different direction of arrival, and different element channel noise. Afterward, the tracking ability of GA-ABF is demonstrated in circumstance where a group of interferences with distinct power change their directions of arrival randomly at certain time interval. Finally, two approaches aimed at improving the effectiveness and rate of convergence of GA-ABF are outlined quantitatively towards suppressing multiple random interferences within the framework of standardized genetic algorithm so that no further complex GA operations is involved.

articleTitle: Analysis of the radiation characteristics of the reflector antenna with surface distortion and holes using PTD
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The reflector antenna distortion model is built by explosion test results. The radiation characteristics of a kind of distorted shaped reflector antenna are computed by using PTD method, and the radiation characteristics of the reflector antenna with holes on the surface are also computed. Good results are achieved, which can provide theoretical guidance for the radar attackers.

articleTitle: Analysis and design of an ultra-wideband nested coaxial waveguide feed
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper a four-cavity 60:1 frequency bandwidth (1-60 GHz) ultra-wideband nested coaxial waveguide feed with extended center conductors is designed and analyzed. The performance of the feed is presented and discussed in detail. The feed has less than -10 dB reflection loss over its operating frequency. The excitation of the coaxial cavities is accomplished by impressing a circularly polarized TE/sub 11/ coaxial waveguide mode. The correlated parameters are rigorously carried out by experimental measurement (1-8 GHz) and a finite element method (FEM) computer simulation study (8-60 GHz).

articleTitle: Combination of genetic algorithm and fast Fourier transform for array failure correction
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: An approach based on a combination of genetic algorithm and fast Fourier transform is presented for array failure correction. It speeds up the evaluation of array pattern by using FFT, so it provides the possibility to speed up the GA. Simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Determination of distributed circuit parameters of non-uniform transmission line by studying the transient behavior of reflected current
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The idea of this paper is that we first construct approximate formulas of the distributed circuit parameter for a non-uniform transmission line, and establish an equivalent distributed circuit. Then, by using time domain method, we can get the current waveforms of the equivalent distributed circuit. In the other hand, we use full wave method to simulate the non-uniform transmission line directly, and obtain another current waveforms of the non-uniform transmission line. By optimizing the coefficients in the approximate formulas, we can obtain a set of coefficients that makes the two current waveforms agree each other, and the formulas arc finally determined. In this paper, a simple example concerning about the extraction of the static inductance and capacitance of the bent two-wire transmission line is given.

articleTitle: Investigation on the performance of a compact microstrip monopulse antenna array
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A microstrip monopulse antenna array has been designed and manufactured. The array, the monopulse comparator and the feed network are placed on the same layer resulting in a very compact structure. But the compact structure may bring some limitations to the improvement of the array performance. In this paper, several factors that affect the array performance are investigated which may serve as the guideline of the design. The -16 dB side lobe level for the sum pattern and 25 dB null depth for the difference pattern have been achieved in the experiment. The simulation and the analysis show that there is still a possibility to improve the array performance.

articleTitle: A microstrip patch antenna on the embedded multi-period EBG structure
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A microstrip patch antenna on a two-dimensional multi-period electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure, embedded between the patch and the ground plane, is proposed and studied in this paper. The impedance bandwidth, radiation pattern and gain of the antennas are assessed using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations and experimental measurements. The simulated and measured results show that the microstrip patch antenna on the sandwiched multiperiod EBG structure can achieve wider impedance bandwidth and higher gain compared to the one on a single period EBG structure. At the same time, the size of the substrate can be reduced substantially.

articleTitle: Coupling of ANNN with GA for effective optimization of dimensions of rectangular patch antenna on thick substrate microstrip patch antenna on thick substrate
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A novel method of optimization by coupling the genetic algorithm (GA) and artificial neural network (ANN) is presented in this paper. A trained artificial neural network is taken as objective function in GA for optimization. By utilizing this technique the optimized dimensions of patch antenna on thick substrate has been calculated. It is seen that the results obtained by this method are closer to experimental value compared to earlier results obtained by curve fitting method. To validate this, the results are compared with experimental values for five fabricated antenna. The results are in very good agreement with experimental findings.

articleTitle: Wideband microstrip monopole slot antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Microstrip antennas have played an important role in the field of wireless communications in the past few decades. It is required in applications such as mobile handsets, PC cards or in PCS, miniaturized as well as wideband antennas. Engineers and researchers have made extensive efforts to miniaturize microstrip antennas, but small antennas inherently have narrow bandwidth. However, in order to transmit and receive more information, large bandwidths are required and bandwidth enhancement is currently a popular research. Some common broadbanding techniques are the use of multimode resonators, use of parasitic elements with main radiating patch and use of stacked patches [R. Garg et al., 2001]. All these techniques result in increasing the antenna size. Therefore, the issue of antenna miniaturization is of major interest [A.K. Skriverik et al., August 2001]. In [(S.K Sharma et al., June 2002) (S.K. Sharma et al.)], a monopole slot cut at one corner of the ground plane was presented with simulated and experimental results. In this paper, the monopole slot at the center of the ground plane is parametrically studied for its impedance bandwidth (S1/sub 1/= -10 dB) using method of moments (MOM) software Ensemble 8.0. The radiation characteristics are also investigated using finite element method (FEM) software, HFSS.

articleTitle: The application of electromagnetic topology in the analysis of HPM effects on system
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper presents an effective method to analyze electromagnetic interfering-electromagnetic topology. It emphasizes on the basic concept of electromagnetic topology and the approximate approach in system analysis. After that, we introduce the application of it in the analysis of HPM effects on the system. Lastly, we use electromagnetic topology to analyze a simple system as an example.

articleTitle: A 3-D ray-propagation multilevel fast multipole algorithm using an adaptive technique
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The 3-D vector electromagnetic scattering problem is solved efficiently by a ray-propagation multilevel fast multipole algorithm (RP-MLFMA). An adaptive technique is developed to control the computational complexity and the accuracy. Numerical results are given to verify the efficiency of the present algorithm.

articleTitle: DOA estimation of ultra-wide band array antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the characteristic of ultra-wideband (UWB) arrays is analyzed in space-time domain and a method of direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation for impulse signal is introduced. This method borrows ideas from signal's cycle stationary characteristic in communication system. By decomposing the output signals' correlation matrix of the UWB arrays, the DOA information is obtained. Simulation result shows that if the cycle frequency isn't high, this method is valid.

articleTitle: Design of a reflector antenna with several sectorial beams for WLL base stations
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A rotationally symmetric reflector antenna with off-axis feeding system is presented to produce a number of sectorial and reconfigurable beams which are useful to be used for base stations in wireless local loop at microwave or millimetric bands.

articleTitle: A prediction model of rain attenuation along Earth-space path
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Rain attenuation is the dominant propagation impairment for satellite communication systems operating at frequencies above about 10 GHz. Based on ITU-R model and experimental cumulative distribution functions of in the database of ITU-R study group 3, a modified method to predict the long-term statistics of the slant-path rain attenuation is proposed where the new rain height model, path adjustment factor and formula for estimating attenuation of other percentages of an average year are developed. Compared with ITU-R model, this model improves the accuracy of rain attenuation prediction.

articleTitle: Unconditionally stable solution for wave equations of the second order
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper reports an unconditionally stable and implicit method to solve the electromagnetic wave equations of the second order numerically without the Courant limit. By using the Crank-Nicolson (CN) scheme with the Douglas-Gunn (DG) algorithm, the numerical solution is second order accurate in both space and time. Two schemes are introduced and compared, and the numerical dispersion relations are given. Numerical experiments agree with the numerical dispersion predicted in theory.

articleTitle: A robust approach for the derivation of closed-form Green's functions for microstrip structures
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A robust approach for the derivation of closed-form Green's functions is considered based upon a three level approximation procedure, which can give more accurate evaluation of the spatial Green's functions even without the advance investigation of the spectral functions in comparison with the previous method.

articleTitle: A 3-dimensional spatial fading correlation model for electromagnetic vector sensors
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A closed-form expression for the spatial fading correlation function between the components of an electromagnetic vector sensor (EVS) in a 3-dimensional multipath channel is derived. The fading correlation function is expressed in terms of both the azimuth and elevation angle of arrival as well as the polarization states of the wave. The results obtained can be used to determine the spatial correlation matrix at both sides of the transmitter and receiver in multiple-input-multiple-output systems. Furthermore, it can be used to predict the system performance of the EVS under various channel conditions. Verification is achieved by comparing with simulation results.

articleTitle: An experimental study on a ground-penetrating radar for detecting water-leaks in buried water transfer pipes
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the feasibility of ground penetrating radar (GPR) probing technology was experimentally investigated. Polyvinyl chloride (PVC) tank filled with dry and homogeneous sand is installed in the laboratory. Within meaningful frequency band of the transmitting signal, the electrical properties of the material under test (MUT), such as dry sand and acryl used in experiment, are measured by using an open-ended coaxial probe method. The electrical properties of the drysand are similar to that of acryl. Therefore, to maintain precise position of the buried targets, support is made of acryl and filled with the dry sand. Leaking water could saturate the surrounding medium of leaky pipes. In experiment, however, it is very difficult to maintain moisture content and distribution of wet sand. Equivalent model instead of wet sand is necessary. The electrical property of the wet sand under saturation is very alike that of methanol. Therefore, the box is made of acryl plates and filled with methanol. The box with methanol filling is equivalently considered as water leakage model. We perform B-scan surveys with various situations. And we have investigated the possibility of GPR on detection water leakage as well as the pipe.

articleTitle: Circular polarization characteristics of one-wavelength L-shaped antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, we propose a circular polarized antenna, which is one-wavelength L-shaped structure with one feed point. The proposed antenna is composed of two elements, which have slightly different length, and the feed point is arranged on the corner point. The length of the two elements is adjusted and the circular polarization characteristics are calculated by using the moment method. As a result, we make clear the principle of the proposed antenna that the circular polarization can be obtained by adjusting design parameters so that the phase difference of excitation currents on the two elements is in agreement with the included angle between the two elements. Moreover, we make an experiment on a fabricated slot type model of the proposed antenna and demonstrated its favorable impedance matching characteristic. The L-shaped and simple feeding structure of the proposed antenna is suited to be built in the corner of front panel of small radio equipment for wireless LAN systems.

articleTitle: An optimization technique for the design of S-band patch antenna array suitable for dual-frequency operation
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper we present the design and optimization approach for the development of S-band microstrip antenna array system with integrated diplexer. The optimization technique using a commercial MoM based solution is discussed in details. The design technique for the microstrip diplexer is also discussed. Measured results display exemplary accuracy with simulated results thereby justifying the use of such techniques for synthesis of antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Design of stacked circular/quasi-elliptical patch array for broadband CP applications
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper presents a design of circularly polarised 4-element planar subarrays composed of low axial-ratio stacked patch elements in X-band. The wideband circular polarisation is excited using stacked circular disc and quasi-elliptical patch that printed on a superstrate with low dielectric constant (/spl epsi/ = 2.2) and a high dielectric constant (/spl epsi/ = 6.15) material as the substrate, respectively. The proposed element exhibits low mutual coupling in two principle planes that is comparable to a single-layer inside the subarray, a pair of microstrip-line fed elements was considered and arranged in four scenarios. Low sidelobe levels and 2-dB axial-ratio bandwidth of 19.5% in addition to a boresight axial-ratio of 0.15 are achieved. Variations in gain and axial ratio other than boresight (/spl theta/ /spl ne/ 0) in azimuth plane are also examined.

articleTitle: Estimation of cross polarization of millimeter waves due to rain over few stations in India and its modification incorporating measured values of rain height
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper an attempt has been made to compute cross polarization of millimeter waves in the 30-35 GHz frequency range due to rain. Assuming Laws and Parson's [Laws JO and Parsons DA, 1943] drop size distributions for oblate spheroid drops at 20 /spl deg/C ITU-R method [ITU-R, 1990] has been used to predict depolarization (XPD) for circular polarization. The study includes a number of earth stations in a temperate country like India, namely, Allahabad, Ahmadabad, Bangalore, Calcutta, Delhi, Gangtok, Jodhpur, Madras, Nagpur and Trivandrum. Variations of co-polar attenuation with XPD ha been shown. Cumulative time distribution of XPD has also been presented. The study reveals that cross polarization depends on frequency, path elevation angle, co-polar attenuation and rainfall rate.

articleTitle: ANDERA: a software tool for the analysis and design of multi-fed and shaped reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A software for the analysis and design of single and dual reflector antennas by physical optics algorithm is presented. The software can also treat user-defined surfaces and feed models for realistic simulation of antenna characteristics. Additionally, array-feed design can be performed.

articleTitle: Wideband scattering of an airfoil with plasma coating
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Using shift operator method, the recursive relation for D/spl I.oarr/ and E/spl I.oarr/ available for FDTD computation of plasma coating is obtained. We apply FDTD and this relation to calculate wideband scattering for an airfoil with plasma coating. To verify the scheme we compute wideband RCS of a circular cylinder with plasma coating, which is in good agreement with the one in literature The computation of airfoil with plasma coating demonstrates the significant reduction of RCS in wideband from 2 - 20 GHz. Based on the results obtained we conjecture that larger electron density and higher electron collision frequency for plasma coating are preferable for the purpose of RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Free-space measurement of bi-axial anisotropic materials
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper presents an extension of the free-space method for measurement of bi-axial anisotropic material at microwave frequencies. In this method, four complex transverse constitutive parameters are directly computed from the reflection and transmission coefficients of a planar sample in free space for a normally incident plane wave with two polarizations. By using the measured amplitudes of the reflection and transmission coefficients of a planar sample at six incident angles with two polarizations, two complex longitudinal constitutive parameters are obtained by finding the solution to minimize the properly designed objective function under the suitable judging criterion. The numerical trials are carried out for a high-loss material by joining random errors to simulate the real measurement condition, which verifies the validity of this method.

articleTitle: Dual-mode patch antenna with PIN diode switch
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Recently, since various wireless communication services such as the PDC, the PHS, and the wireless LAN are provided, it is required to make a mobile terminal to handle several wireless communication services. Generally, these services operate at different frequencies with different polarization and radiation characteristics. Therefore, it is necessary to design a multi-mode antenna which has multi-frequency band and different polarization and radiation pattern at each band, and the switching of the resonant modes should be controlled electronically. In this research, a dual-mode patch antenna is proposed where a PIN diode switch is used to change the resonant mode of the antenna. The characteristics of the antenna, such as the resonant frequency, radiation pattern, and the radiation efficiency are investigated experimentally and numerically.

articleTitle: A microstrip antenna element for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper gives a detailed analysis on the impedance and radiating characteristics of a micro-strip patch antenna by computer simulation. Some relationships between its size and characteristic parameters have been found. A new structure of micro-strip antenna is presented based on the analysis, which can be used in VSAT station and satisfied with the following requirement of C-band satellite communication: dual-frequency, wide-band, dual-polarization and isolation. The result gives a good accordance with the conclusion presented in the simulation.

articleTitle: Analyses of directivity function characteristics channel mismatch correction for DBF in subarray
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: We analyze the directivity functions of DBF in subarray under the ideal condition and with channel mismatch, and give the sum and difference directivity functions. We correct the reception channel mismatch by using the channel equalization method. The way, based on the principle of inverse filtering for recovering the ideal signals, can be realized both in time domain and in frequency domain. The method can correct the mismatch inside a channel and among channels, and is also suitable for both DBF in array element and DBF in subarray. Both of the analyses and the simulation results demonstrate that the method is fairly effective.

articleTitle: The influence of communication distance on multipath channel characteristic of tunnel
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Ray-tracing method was used to simulate the characteristic of wide band radio wave transmission in tunnel. The simulation results showed that the root-mean-square delay spread /spl tau//sub rms/ caused by multipath propagation fade varied with the communication distance in tunnel. Therefore the correlation bandwidth of the channel was connected with the communication distance in tunnel. The attenuation caused by multipath propagation fade varied with the communication distance too.

articleTitle: Characterization of (Co-Mn-Ti) substituted M type barium hexagonal ferrite based microwave absorber at X band
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper present the design, development and characterization of the hexagonal ferrite powder [BaCo/sub 0.5/spl delta//Ti/sub 0.5/spl delta//Mn/sub 0.1/Fe(11.87-/spl delta/)O/sub 19/] at /spl delta/=1.6 as microwave absorber. The hexagonal ferrite powder has been developed by dry attrition and sintering procedure. The developed ferrite powder 60% by weight has been mixed in epoxy resin to form a microwave absorbing paint. This paint was coated on conducting aluminum sheet to study absorption characteristics of linearly polarized TE wave at X band. The experimental and computed results for different coating thickness have been reported. It has been found that it shows the broadband characteristics with minimum absorption of 6.5 dB from 8 to 12 GHz for a coating thickness of 2 mm. These paints are very useful in military application such as RCS reduction, camouflaging of the target and prevention of EMI etc.

articleTitle: Analyses and compensation for radar target angular glint
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Angular glint caused by a target of dual point sources is discussed in phase gradient method. Deterministic relation between phase gradient and RCS is deduced. On the basis of that, a RCS based compensation method of angular glint is presented. The validity is verified by simulation. For target of multi-point sources, compensation for angular glint error is similar if it is treated as a target of dual point sources.

articleTitle: Analysis of omnidirectional waveguide slots array antennas
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper proposes a new approach for analyzing waveguide slots and their arrays. It considers the whole waveguide structure with slots cut on conducting walls as a complete antenna system. Based on this idea, the electric field integral equation (EFIE) is formulated in a standard way, and the integral equation is then solved using the method of moments where the Rao, Wilton and Glisson (RWG) functions are employed as both basis and weighting functions in the Galerkin's procedure. With the scheme implemented, longitudinal slot-pairs cut on the broad-wall are analyzed and their results newly obtained and discussed. The computed results theoretically show that the broad-wall longitudinal single slot-pair and slot-pair array can produce very good omnidirectional patterns in the E-plane.

articleTitle: The transient radiation of thin circular loop antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the points on the thin circular loop antenna is excited by the step current pulse synchronously, so that the loop antenna can be considered as a magnetic dipoles disk which is formed by vertical magnetic dipoles. By means of analytic integral, the analytic representations of the vector potentials associated with the thin circular loop antenna are obtained, and then, the relationship between the pulse width of the field and the location of the observer has been analyzed. The analysis indicate that the pulse width of the field is broadened with increasing the plunge angle of the observer, and, when the shadow of the observer is inside the disk, the pulse width of the field is also broadened with increasing the offset distance of the observer and tend to a finite value 2a sin/spl Theta//c . The analytic expression also indicate that the field pulse can be considered as radiated by the points which are on a diameter of the circular loop, meanwhile, the pulse width is equal to the difference of the wave arrival time from the two points which are the farthest and the nearest point from the observer on the diameter to the observer.

articleTitle: A novel technique for the determination of the radiation patterns of medium gain antennas from scalar intensity measurements
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This work described a technique whereby indirect holography can be extended to enable the radiation patterns of medium gain antennas to be obtained in a simple and inexpensive manner. It has described a method which overcomes the limitations imposed by using a traditional radiated reference signal. This has been achieved by sampling at spacing much less than half wavelength and electronically introducing a phase shift between each sample. The resultant separation of Fourier transform terms enables the far field radiation pattern to be determined. This has been supported by simulation results for a small antenna which demonstrate the improvement available using this technique. It has also demonstrated that this technique can also be applied to the reconstruction of complex fields at any desired distance from the antenna. This has included the reconstruction of antenna aperture fields which show good agreement with the original aperture fields.

articleTitle: A new realizable technique to improve the VCO linearity
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper is presented a new technique to improve the VCO linearity by resampling the measured IF signal in short-range frequency modulated continuous wave (FM/CW) radar based on a known reflecting reference, which caused intentionally by a specially fabricated paraboloidal antenna. The basic principle and special attention are given in following discussion. Moreover, a confirmed experiment in microwave non-reflective chamber is simulated. The result shows the feasibility of our self-made antenna and this method satisfactorily.

articleTitle: A hybrid 2-D ADI-FDTD subgridding scheme
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method gives accurate results but uses a large amount of computer memory and time, which can be reduced by applying higher resolution only around critical areas in the problem domain. In this paper, a new subgridding scheme have been proposed which based on the hybridization of the alterative-direction implicit FDTD (ADI-FDTD) and FDTD algorithms. The field components in fine local grids are updated using the ADI-FDTD method, and in the coarse main grids conventional FDTD method is utilized. The technique achieves the same time marching step in the whole domain as employed in the coarse FDTD scheme, and the need for the temporal interpolation of the fields in the fine grids is obviated since the ADI-FDTD scheme is unconditionally stable. Hence, the hybrid ADI-FDTD subgridding scheme is less time consuming and easy to implement. Practical applications of the algorithm in the simulations of the scattering of conducting cylinder and dielectric square cylinder are reported.

articleTitle: A simplified CFDTD algorithm for scattering analysis
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The scattering calculation may be inaccurate while the conventional FDTD method in cartesian coordinates uses staircase approximation to model curvilinear surface. In tins paper, a simplified conformal FDTD (CFDTD) scheme is presented to overcome staircase error. Although the areas and lengths of the distorted cells are also employed in the same way of the previous CFDTD algorithm, this scheme uses a radio of 1/6 (the distorted cell area to the regular cell area) as a criterion to eliminate instability due to the very small distorted cell sizes To show the validity and applicable of the presented scheme, computed RCS's are compared with that from the conventional FDTD. other methods and measured values.

articleTitle: Estimation of mutual coupling coefficient by simulated annealing algorithm
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method for estimating the mutual coupling coefficient among antennas, which is based on the principle of signal subspace and the simulated annealing algorithm. The computer simulation have been conducted to illustrate the good performance of this method and to demonstrate that it is statistically efficient. The benefit of this new method is that calibration signals and unknown signals can be received simultaneously, during the course of calibration.

articleTitle: Study on the algorithm of real eigenvalue decompositions with a uniform circular array
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The paper focuses on the improved 2-D MUSIC algorithm that operates in beamspace for DOA estimation with a uniform circular array (UCA). The algorithm requires only real eigenvalue decompositions to obtain noise subspace estimates, so that it has many advantages, including reduced amount of computation and enhanced precision, especially in a series of dual coherent sources scenarios. These excellent performances are verified by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Virtual rays for diffraction coefficients of a composite wedge
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: This paper presents a new concept of virtual rays has been suggested for constructing diffraction coefficients of a composite wedge. Basically, the suggested method plays an important role in obtaining diffraction coefficients of some penetrable wedges in closed form. The uniform currents induced on the wedge interfaces were derived from the GO field. The complete PO solution could be obtained analytically by applying the uniform currents into the dual integral equations. The error of the obtained PO solution was interpreted by nonzeroness of the artificial field emanating from the uniform currents in the complementary regions, in which the media inside and outside dielectric wedge are exchanged with each other. The concept of complementary regions may be considered as an extension of the null-field method or the extended boundary conditions.

articleTitle: The developments of smart antenna system at Da Yeh University
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The effects of multiple paths and channel capacity are concerned in the communication system. The SAS (smart antenna system) can solve these problems. The SAS can be separated by adaptive antenna array and MBA (multiple beams antenna array). In this paper, the MBA is discussed. There are different types of SAS that are developed in Taiwan for the applications of cellular phone system in GSM, WCDMA, and WLAN (wireless local access network). Key components such as wideband RP radiators and different kinds of RF BFN are developed for SAS. Several types of SAS with multiple beams and narrower beamwidth are developing and testing at Da Yeh University. The test results are quite agreed with that of simulation.

articleTitle: Improvement of the accuracy in FDTD analysis of printed rectangular antennas by using quasi-static approximation
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the improvement of FDTD calculation accuracy for printed antennas is proposed. The quasi-static approximation of electromagnetic field was incorporated into the FDTD update equation by using the integral form of the Faraday's law. A few examples of the printed antennas were analyzed by using the proposed method, and the significant improvement of the calculation accuracy has been achieved even if the same cell size as original FDTD is used. Furthermore, the validity of proposed method for antenna sets incline for FDTD cell is also indicated.

articleTitle: A new type of X-band data transmission antenna used on CBERS-1 satellite
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In consideration of poor space of mounting plan towards the Earth and some technical reasons, the shaped reflector will not be recommended to use for the CBERS-1 satellite, therefore a backfire helical antenna occupied a small space is adapted for IR-MSS data transmission antenna(DTA) on the CBERS-1 instead of the shaped reflector. The antenna's performance and function is similar to that of the shaped reflector. The design of the antenna and its performances will be briefly described in the paper. At first, it describes the ideal coverage curve and engineering model of the coverage gain for data transmission antenna on the low-orbit satellite. The paper then gives the mathematical model of radiation of the antenna, the characteristic equation for propagation constant is developed in the section. Using complex propagation constant of the helical antenna a saddle shaped beam, whose maximum pointing at 62.5/spl deg/ has been designed. Main properties and function of IR-MSS DTA on the CBERS-1 are then briefly introduced. The antenna possesses compact structure, small size, flight weight and low cost besides the similar performance to the shaped reflector. It is also more suitable for a variety of small satellites or micro satellites.

articleTitle: The influence of scattering on multipath channel characteristic of tunnel
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Scattering that influences the multipath propagation characteristic in tunnel is discussed. Simulations for both with and without scattering are made to demonstrate the mechanism of the scattering effects on multipath propagation. During the simulation two different carrier frequencies are used to illustrate how the roughness of the tunnel affects the multipath propagation.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of an X-band corrugated feed horn for offset reflector antenna
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Satellite communication and remote sensing systems need reflector antennas for communication. An efficient system could be constructed with offset reflector and an appropriate corrugated horn to generate low cross polarization, high efficiency, low VSWR and low side lobe level. An offset reflector antenna has been designed and an appropriate corrugated horn in X-band satellite communication with near perfect Gaussian beam was constructed to achieve the required specifications.

articleTitle: An on-line array calibration method for the DS-CDMA system
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this article, an eigenstructure-based on-line calibration method is presented to estimate the array channel gain and phase parameters. By employing the characteristics of the DS-CDMA system, the calibration can be carried out while the system is working. So it is quite suitable for the practical application. It first estimates the initial parameters by an iteration algorithm, and then use the subspace tracking method to trace the changes of the gain and phase parameters in real-time. The proposed algorithm is described in detail, and numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and behavior of the calibration method.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling between linear dipoles in an array environment
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The influence of parasitic elements to self and mutual impedance is found through the idea of generalized impedance matrix in this paper. Extra ports are defined on the element to take into account the surface current on the open-circuited parasitic elements. A 3 by 3 array of dipole antenna is analyzed to verify the efficiency of this method. The idea might also be extended to analyze arrays of microstrip patch antennas.

articleTitle: Solving 3-D electromagnetic scattering from conducting object by MLFMA with curvilinear RWG basis
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) with curvilinear RWG basis is used to realize fast, accurate solution of electromagnetic scattering from 3-D conducting object. This method needs much less unknowns than traditional RWG basis and conformal rooftop basis, is especially appropriate for efficient solution of scattering from target with large electrical sizes. Numerical results are given to demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the present method.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis of radiation from monopole antenna with plasma coating
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: To analyze the radiation of a monopole covered with plasma, a shift operator method in FDTD is applied. By using this scheme we compute the radiation of a monopole antenna with the coverage of plasma. We observe from the numerical results that the plasma can greatly absorb electromagnetic waves and can impede the Gaussian pulse travelling along the antenna. In addition, the high frequency components in the radiation fields are decreased, and the resonant frequencies are shifted.

articleTitle: Low profile parasitic antenna array of monopole by using dielectric resonator ring
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Using a dielectric resonator ring around the monopole to reduce the profile of the parasitic antenna array, it is shown that less than 50% of the original height can be achieved, and a parasitic array with a dielectric ring for each monopole is studied.

articleTitle: Light scattering property of fractal soot particles
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Based on the fundamental conception of fractal. We simulate fractal like clusters of spheres. Calculations are performed on these spheres, which refractive index values arc characteristic of carbonaceous soot in the visible wavelengths. The T matrix approach together with the translation addition theorem for vector spherical waves is employed to solve the aggregate scattering problem. Numerical results for scattering matrix are illustrated for fractal clusters. And the sensitivity of scattering matrix diagram to optical characteristics of fractal-like soot agglomerates is discussed.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of array antennas for mobile handsets
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the radiation characteristics of array antennas affected by the element configuration, the size of the ground plate are studied by using the FDTD method. The scan patterns for several arrays are investigated in details in order to determine which configuration is more suitable to the array antenna for mobile handset. Furthermore, the XPD in the scan plane is calculated to understand the scan properties of the arrays. Finally, the effect of the ground size on the radiation pattern of array antenna is investigated in order to decide the optimum size of the ground plate for the beam control of the arrays.

articleTitle: Study on the electromagnetic scattering from the fractal surface with considering the shadowing effect
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Based on the Kirchhoff approximation for rough surface scattering and by calculating the shadowing function of the rough surface, the formula of the scattering cross section of the fractal rough surface is present with consideration of the shadowing effect. The influence of the shadowing effect on the bistatic scattering cross section for different fractal dimension and fundamental spatial frequency is discussed in detail.

articleTitle: EMI antenna calibration using the antenna impedance measurement
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A newly developed EMI antenna calibration method named antenna impedance method is theoretically investigated on the antenna arrangements and the attainable accuracy. This calibration method requires only antenna impedance measurements on an antenna under calibration above a metal ground plane at various antenna heights. The paper briefly reviews the theoretical basis of the method and the experimental results obtained by this method. Then, an appropriate height range for the antenna scanning is investigated by using the method of moments. In addition, the achievable accuracy of this calibration method is evaluated by taking into account the error in antenna impedance measurements. It is concluded that the accuracy of the antenna impedance method is around 0.3 dB or less for the almost all frequencies from 30 to 1000 MHz. It is comparable to the standard antenna method that is commonly used for EMI antenna calibration at many national standard institutes.

articleTitle: The antenna test facilities at Da Yeh University
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the hybrid near field antenna measurement system and ITDAMS (impulse time domain antenna measurement system) at Da Yeh University are presented. The hybrid near field antenna test ranges with scan types of spherical, cylindrical, and planar can test the antennas with different kinds of directivity. The ITDAMS is for principal planes measurement. The ITDAMS is for higher directivity and larger size of antenna measurement. The test results from both systems are quite agreed.

articleTitle: Gratinglobe suppression of phased array antenna for mobile satellite communications
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A gratinglobe suppression technique of phased array antenna using an angular spatial filter is described. Angular spatial filter can be added to the existing antenna in order to reduce gratinglobes of the antenna. Based on microwave theory and EM analysis, an angular spatial filter is designed. The designed angular spatial filter has the power level lower 17 dB around /spl plusmn/ 50/spl deg/ from the main beam, ripple /spl plusmn/ 1.5 dB, and pass angle 20/spl deg/ at 12.25 GHz on TE case and power level lower 15 dB, ripple /spl plusmn/ 1.4 dB, and pass angle 27/spl deg/ at 12.25 GHz on TM case in satellite communication In this paper the measured results are shown to be not bad in the gratinglobe suppression. The designed filter is applicable for the reduction of gratinglobes for the phased array antenna system and radome of beamforming antenna.

articleTitle: Analysis of the characteristic of rainfall attenuation of microwave and calculation module simulation
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, we present the newest calculation model of microwave propagation attenuation by rainfall in atmosphere, simulate the rainfall attenuation in a certain area according to its weather data and geography information system, and analyze the simulation results simply.

articleTitle: A novel piecewise algorithm for reconstructing 2-D uniform samples from 2-D bipolar non-uniform ones for planar near-field antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In order to compute the far field pattern of an antenna from its near field samples, uniform sampling techniques have been widely used. If a signal is non-uniformly sampled due to bi-polar method, the reconstruction of far field can not be obtained directly. Here we proposed a novel, fast interpolation method that recovers the uniformly spaced samples of near field from the unequally spaced ones which are gathered through bipolar method.

articleTitle: Estimation of strip-line losses in printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: As computer processing speeds increase into the GHz frequencies, the dielectric and conductor losses in a strip-line, which are negligible at data rates below 1 Gbps, become increasingly important as they lead to a decline in signal integrity. The dielectric losses of printed circuit boards (PCBs) are computed from measured loss tangent values, which are very small and whose accuracy is not clearly defined. Therefore, a more accurate generalized model of a slightly lossy dielectric is needed to better estimate losses. As measured values of the real permittivity component are more accurate, they can be used to estimate the lossy component using a modified form of the Kramers-Kronig relations. Using Collin's relationships for a strip-line, the conductor losses are estimated. The sum of these theoretically calculated losses for TEM propagation agreed well with measured losses for short strip-lines in PCBs, from 100 MHz to 6 GHz. It is also seen that there is a comparatively small deviation of 1.97 dB for higher frequencies (6-14 GHz).

articleTitle: An improved genetic algorithm optimizing microstrip filter with equal width
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: When design band-pass filter of parallel coupled microstrip lines with equal width using cascading method, it is necessary to adjust some parameters and validate the results repeatedly, and it is difficult to determine the optimum parameters. The combination of an improved genetic algorithms and the cascading method is presented in this paper. The optimal parameters can be obtained through the combined method only needing running a program. At last an example verifies the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Diffraction at edges in planar impedance surfaces: revisited exact solutions at skew incidence
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the revisited exact solutions are presented for the electromagnetic problems of a half plane with surface impedance faces and a surface impedance edge discontinuity on a plane, when they are illuminated at skew incidence. They are obtained by introducing a suitable new set of combined spectra that exhibit all the desired properties. As a consequence, the final expressions of the spectra satisfy all the Malyuzhinets method conditions, the edge conditions, explicitly satisfy reciprocity and nicely reduce to the original Malyuzhinets solution for normal incidence. The importance of the achieved symmetry with respect to incidence and observation aspects, is further emphasized in extending the solutions to dipole source illuminations.

articleTitle: Analysis of pulsed signal distortion in microstrip line using Wigner-Ville distribution
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Wigner-Ville distribution (WVD) is used to analyze the propagation of pulse traveling in microstrip lines. Characteristics of Gaussian pulse are studied on their zoom-in time-amplitude windows, fast Fourier transforms, and time-frequency results. FDTD method is used to get the waveform of Gaussian pulse signal propagating in microstrip line, and then WVD technique can be used to observe the distortion locally at any time and at any point in the microstrip line and is especially attractive to the microstrip line with complex structure, which can be analyzed by FDTD.

articleTitle: Facet noise in RCS prediction
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The facet noise in RCS prediction is studied in this paper. Faster speed of computation and higher accuracy is obtained with a proper facet model build. The number of facets needed to model a target increases with the size of the target and the frequency of the incident wave. The criterion of facetization is discussed and some helpful results are obtained.

articleTitle: Multi band, multi antenna system for modern mobile terminal
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A compact, multi-band, multi antenna system was designed and optimized. It has compact size, good performance, good isolation and is very cost effective. MoM is successfully used in the antenna design and optimization. The results agree well with the measurements. The extension of the antenna work was done, to have this kind of antenna system as a GSM/DCS/PCS/UMTS version and a 850/900/1800/1900 quad-band version as well.

articleTitle: Cylindrical periodic structures of metallic wires
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: First, we calculate the total field for an outgoing or an incoming TM cylindrical incident wave illuminating a cylindrical periodic structure of metallic wires. Then, we give analytical formulas to extract the characteristics (reflection and transmission) of the cylindrical periodic structure. To finish, we extend the study to infinite radius periodic structure by given an approximation of the dispersion diagram.

articleTitle: A compact microstrip patch antenna with T-shaped slits for portable GPS handsets
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, a compact patch antenna with T-shape slits fed by crossed aperture coupling is proposed for miniaturized portable GPS handsets. The results of embedded T-slits for compact antenna size show that the resonant frequency is significantly lowered from 2.845 GHz to 1.675 GHz. corresponding to a 44.65% antenna size reduction compared to reference design. Experimental results show that good CP radiation patterns are obtained and impedance bandwidth (VSWR 2), 3 dB axial ratio are about 21 MHz, 17 MHz at the center resonant frequency, respectively.

articleTitle: Novel specific absorption rate (SAR) measurement system using flat-plane solid phantom
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the required dimensions of the flat-plane solid phantom are derived using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to obtain detailed SAR measurements that are equivalent to standardized procedures using the liquid. The proposed measurement system using the flat-plane solid phantom constructed using ceramic materials is presented and the system is validated by acquiring SAR distributions at 900 MHz for two types of antennas.

articleTitle: Comparison of reflection and transmission performances for different parameters of 2-dimensional dielectric periodic structures
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the finite element method incorporated with Floquet theorem is used to solve the 2-dimensional scattering problem of dielectric periodic structures that a plane wave is oblique or perpendicular incident. Comparisons of reflection and transmission properties for a kind of dielectric photonic crystals with different structure parameters are presented.

articleTitle: A numerical pattern synthesis algorithm for arbitrary arrays
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, a numerical method for antenna array pattern synthesis is presented. By this method, the designer can efficiently verify mainlobe shaping, null steering and sidelobe levels. When a large number of interfering signals occurred at various angles throughout the sidelobe region, the sidelobes are controlled by an iterative method based on adaptive array theory. The values of the weighting function in the L/sub 2/ norm, interpreted as imaginary jammers, and are iterated to minimize exceedance of the desired sidelobe levels and minimize the absolute difference between desired and achieved mainlobe patterns. Simulation examples, including both nonuniform linear and planar arrays, are shown to illustrate the effective of this method.

articleTitle: Characteristics of the broadband cylindrically conformal microstrip antennas with capacitance compensation probe feed
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The input impedance and the radiation pattern of the stacked cylindrically conformal microstrip patch antenna element with capacitance compensation probe feed and the mutual coupling effect between two elements of this kind are calculated by using a novel hybrid method that combines the conformal FDTD method and the Green's functions for cylindrically stratified media. Numerical results demonstrate that about 29% or more impedance bandwidth can be achieved when VSWR/spl les/2.0 by using this structure.

articleTitle: Evaluation and acceleration of Sommerfeld integrals for stratified media Green's functions
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Several efficient methods are proposed in this paper to evaluate and accelerate the Sommerfeld integrals for stratified media Green's functions, with the emphasis on the case of half-space. For reference, the slowly convergent method of integration along the Sommerfeld integration path (SIP) is first summarily discussed. To speed up the convergence of the SIs, the deformation is made from the SIP to the steepest descent path (SDP). If branch point is surrounded by the contour, the constant phase path passing through the branch point (BSDP) is added to calculate the contribution of the branch point singularity. Along the deformed path, the integrands have a characteristic of constant phase and fast decaying, which results in the contribution of the path integration mainly from the vicinity of the saddle point and the computation time reduced. Further reducing computation time is realized through the asymptotic approximation based stationary phase method or saddle point method (SPA) along the SDP or the BSDP and physical explanation is enlightened. Numerical results show the validity of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Antenna array self-calibration algorithm with sensor location errors
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The antenna array characteristics like sensor location, gain and phase response are rarely perfectly known in realistic situations. Self-calibration algorithms estimate both source DOAs and perturbed array response vector parameters simultaneously. In this paper calibration errors are usually assumed Io be small and a first order approximation to the perturbed array response vector is often used to simplify the estimation procedure. We introduce two classes of self-calibration algorithms for solving the sensor location error problem. This paper investigates the performance of these algorithms. Simulation results show that iterative approach and MAP-NSF algorithm are much better than MUSIC algorithm, and the iterative approach is preferred. But the iterative approach is very sensitive to initialization. A novel algorithm, using the MAP-NSF algorithm results as the input to the iterative approach, is proposed to eliminate sensor location errors and remove the sensitivity to initialization. Further simulation results demonstrate the improved performance of the new approach.

articleTitle: Analysis on oceanic and terrestrial domino effect of atmosphere refractive
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, we have utilized the set of recently five years meteorologic profiles sounding made in five representative areas along the coast of southeast China and applied mode of subsection to calculate statistically refractive index. Based on former work, analysis on oceanic and terrestrial domino effect of atmosphere refractive has been carried through using graph coming from statistic data, and standard deviation has also been obtained by least mean square (LMS).

articleTitle: The application of PML-FDTD and boundary consistency conditions of total-scattered fields in three dimension cylindrical coordinates
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, the finite-difference time-domain formation of Maxwell's equation in perfectly matched layer (PML-FDTD) is deduced in three dimensional (3-D) cylindrical complex stretched coordinates. In order to investigate the scattering characteristics of cylindrical objects by using cylindrical FDTD method, the boundary consistency conditions of total-scattered fields are proposed in 3-D cylindrical complex stretched coordinates, Further, planar wave excitation sources are set on the boundaries by using one dimension (1-D) FDTD and linear interpolation method so as to simulate the propagation of plane (TEM) wave in free space. The far-field scattering patterns of a hollow cylinder are computed when it exited by a TEM wave.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the performance of indoor MIMO systems
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: From a system point of view, the capacity and diversity are the two main characteristics afforded by the multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) systems. The increasing of capacity of multiple-input-multiple-output space-time system seriously relies on the richness of multipath rays which provide uncorrelated or low-correlated parallel sub-channels. The investigation of performance of indoor MIMO systems using one correlated model presented in this paper shows that the arrangements of antenna array elements as well as the indoor scattering environment influence the spatial cross correlation which in turn influences the system performance. The results of investigation provide insights on the design of indoor space-time systems.

articleTitle: On study of a new patch antenna with macromolecule magnetic substrate
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: A new patch antenna with macromolecule magnetic substrate is presented in this paper. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results showed that this kind of patch antenna has extremely wide frequency bandwidth for the impedance character.

articleTitle: Optical integrated circuits application in medicine
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: ASlC is the "Mantra" among today's electronic engineers. To make a major impact in the integrated circuit arena, it is essential to find a way to add functionally to silicon devices. Such is the aim of the optical application specific integrated circuit (OASIC) research. The photosensitive property of silicon is used in advance imaging technology through "smart pixel" sensors. The heart of an OASIC chip is poly-si because it is a wavelength-sensitive reflector, absorber and transmitter of light.

articleTitle: Analysis of beam tilting behaviour for the measurement of EUT radiating slots
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, beam tilting behavior of radiating slots is introduced. When the radiating field intensity is measured in EMI/EMC test, the receiving antenna or probe must be moved along its vertical axis because of its beam tilting behavior. The radiation pattern is measured by near-field measurement system and verified by the finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The far-field pattern was obtained from near far field transformation by using near-field data. The beam tilted about 18 /spl deg/ at 10.82 GHz and the FDTD method provides a good result to this measurement.

articleTitle: A method for adaptive anti-interference based on subarrays in HF ground wave radar
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: To improve the capability of high frequency (HF) surface wave radar to suppress interference, an adaptive anti-interference technique was evaluated by using subarrays in OSMAR2000 (ocean state monitor and analysis radar, manufactured in 2000). In this paper, we put forward a scheme to suppress the external HF radio strong interference based on OSMAR2000 radar without increasing any accessional facilities, and some radar experiments were carried out by using a monopole as main antenna and other three vertical monopoles as auxiliary antennas. This paper presented the results of a preliminary study of an adaptive system with subarrays for the suppression of strong interference. The results of the study show that the technique worked well against the observed interference.

articleTitle: The analysis of the air breakdown threshold power of high power microwave
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In this paper, theoretical research on the air breakdown threshold of high power microwave pulse propagating in atmosphere is derived approximately. Some new views are presented about the existed questions of air breakdown.

articleTitle: Effect of space diversity technique in UHF band radio indoor propagation
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: In order to clarify the receiving condition in the whole room, in this paper, the received level contour map is created based on the measured data of the UHF band radio wave in the indoor environment. Moreover, this paper investigates the effects of applying the space diversity technique that have been well known to be effective techniques to improve the deep fading considering the space uncorrelation of the received level (M. Schwartz et al.) By use of the measured level data, in order to clarify the space diversity effects in the indoor environments, the correlation coefficients between two branches and the cumulative probabilities of the received level are evaluated in case that the space diversity techniques with selection combining are applied.

articleTitle: Three dimensional packaging and interconnecting techniques for microwave modules
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: Three dimensional (3D) packaging and interconnecting techniques can greatly reduce the weight and volume of conventional planar microwave modules. The objective of this study was to employ a novel 3D structure with simple manufacturing process to develop 3D microwave modules. Many advanced 3D packaging and interconnecting methods, such as LTCC microwave multichip modules, vertical interconnects, and 3D electromagnetic field analyzing and optimizing, were applied to increase the package density and improve the electric performance. Test method and test results of 3D microwave modules were introduced. These techniques are very useful to many types of modern active phased array radar systems and communication systems.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of a patch antenna with shorting posts
publicationTitle: 6th International SYmposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory, 2003. Proceedings. 2003
abstract: The finite element method (FEM) is applied to analyze a thin substrate antenna with shorting posts. The numerical results of the resonant frequencies are found in good agreement with the experimental data.
